# NeuroMechFly reference anatomy

Source: NeLy-EPFL/FlyGym, https://github.com/NeLy-EPFL/flygym

Pinned source revision: `38c8ec61034cd59bc5ba0de20688d4a3c0000d60`.

License: Apache License, Version 2.0. The unmodified license is included as `LICENSE`.

Source files: `src/flygym/assets/model/neuromechfly/meshes/simplified_max2000faces/*.stl`, `rigging.yaml`, and `pose/neutral/yaw_pitch_roll.yaml`; kinematic topology and axis conventions checked against `src/flygym/anatomy.py`, `src/flygym/compose/fly/base_fly.py`, and `src/flygym/compose/pose.py` at the pinned revision.

Model provenance: NeuroMechFly is based on micro-CT morphology of an adult female *Drosophila melanogaster*. This is a scientific reference model, not a reconstruction of the individual's anatomy in a user photograph. Study: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41592-024-02497-y ; documentation: https://neuromechfly.org/ .

Derived files: `fly-rig.json`, `fly-rig.json.gz`, `fly-rig-skeleton.json`, generated by `convert-assets.cjs`. Modifications: converted source STL vertex coordinates from meters to millimeters; indexed shared vertices; rounded vertices to 0.000001 mm; encoded topology, normalized XYZW quaternions, anatomical joint axes and mirrored neutral angles as JSON. Source biological geometry was not sculpted or replaced. The 39 unique meshes instantiate 69 segments (115,158 triangles).

Animation offsets supplied by the containing application are illustrative. They are not recorded courtship dance or a physics simulation, unless the application independently implements and verifies those processes.

## Integration

The JSON top level contains `metadata`, `geometries`, and `bodies`.

Each geometry has `positions` (flat XYZ array, already mm) and `indices` (triangle vertex index array). Build an indexed Three.js BufferGeometry and compute vertex normals. Do not recenter each geometry: its local origin is the anatomical joint.

Each body has `name`, `parent`, `mesh`, `mirrorY`, `pos`, `quat`, `joints`, and `restQuat`. Bodies are listed in parent-before-child order. Create one Group per body; position it with `pos`. Set its orientation to `quat` and multiply the ordered axis-angle rotations for each joint using `joint.rest + animationOffset`. `restQuat` is the precomputed result at zero animation offset. All quaternions are XYZW. All angles are radians. For right side meshes, set only the child Mesh scale to `[1, -1, 1]`; the hierarchy, axes and positions are already mirrored. A Three.js Mesh with negative Y scale handles winding; if mirroring vertices manually, reverse triangle winding.

Source axes: +X forward, +Y fly-left, +Z up. FlyGym names leg yaw as X rotation, pitch as Y rotation, roll as Z rotation. Right yaw and roll axes are explicitly negated. Do not substitute conventional aircraft Euler axes. `joints` are ordered yaw, pitch, roll (omitting unsupported axes); multiplying them in that sequence preserves the official neutral pose.

For a conventional Y-up Three.js world, place the whole rig under an outer Group rotated by -PI/2 about X. Source +Z then becomes world +Y. The source root thorax has a height of 1.3 mm. The official neutral pose is a pre-simulation joint initialization, so its feet do not all touch a flat plane without settling; minimum source-space vertex height is -0.07425 mm. Floor placement or a small whole-rig tilt/offset is a presentation choice.

Non-leg segments are independently attached at source anatomical origins. FlyGym's ALL_BIOLOGICAL preset permits three rotation axes for these connections; the dataset does not provide measured dance trajectories or calibrated motion limits for them. The app may animate head, wings and abdomen at these pivots, but should identify this as illustrative articulation.
